name: fIREHOSE
label: SST
lede: A grieving bass player, a drummer with nothing to drum for, and a 21-year-old from Ohio who wouldn't stop calling: 980 gigs later, it turned out to be a band.

eras.title: The kid who kept calling
eras.text: After D. Boon died, Mike Watt and George Hurley had no band and no plan to start one. An Ohio college kid chasing a false rumor changed that, and within months the three were playing shows under a name borrowed from a Bob Dylan film.

q: This guy kept calling me up, kept calling and calling.
years.h: Ed Crawford hears a false rumor and calls Mike Watt
years.p: [[Ed Crawford|c02f03fe-93cf-4590-841b-1b9f04d6a694]], a 21-year-old Ohio State student, hears Minutemen's survivors are auditioning guitarists. They aren't. He gets Mike Watt's number at a Columbus show and calls anyway.
years.xp:
Crawford had come out of a Minutemen show saying he'd rarely been so moved by a live band. Watt, still grieving, kept saying no. Crawford flew to Southern California and kept asking to jam; right before he was due back in Ohio, Watt gave in.

At the San Pedro tryout Crawford played [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]]'s 'I'm One' and Minutemen songs. Watt and [[George Hurley|e3644b83-1c19-41fa-bf81-483551cd1588]] asked him to join.

years.h: Ed Crawford moves to San Pedro and sleeps under Mike Watt's desk
years.p: Now 'ed fROMOHIO', Crawford spends nine months sleeping under a desk in Mike Watt's one-bedroom apartment.

years.h: The name comes from Bob Dylan; the lowercase f is for Minutemen
years.p: fIREHOSE takes its name from Bob Dylan's 'Subterranean Homesick Blues' film clip. The lowercase f is a quiet nod to the all-caps MINUTEMEN logo.

years.h: First fIREHOSE gig: San Pedro, June 1986
years.p: Six months after D. Boon's death, Mike Watt and George Hurley are back on a hometown stage with [[Ed Crawford|c02f03fe-93cf-4590-841b-1b9f04d6a694]].

years.h: On the road with Sonic Youth's Flaming Telepaths Tour
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], who'd pulled Mike Watt out of his grief by putting him on EVOL, take fIREHOSE out on their Flaming Telepaths Tour.

years.h: Ragin', Full-On: fIREHOSE's first album on SST
years.p: Rockers like 'Choose Any Memory' next to quiet pieces like 'The Candle and the Flame'. Trouser Press heard a prickly integrity that honored D. Boon without imitating him.

eras.title: Records to promote tours
eras.text: fIREHOSE lived in the van. They toured more than they recorded, turned up in skateboard videos, and on their third album found a warmer, country-tinged sound that finally sounded like no one but them.

years.h: If'n: Ed Crawford steps up, and R.E.M. gets parodied
years.p: Crawford leads on 'Anger', the band slips in a parody of [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]], and Mike Watt contributes a spoken-word piece.

years.h: Mike Watt marries Black Flag bassist Kira Roessler
years.p: [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] marries [[Kira Roessler|2c65be73-5658-47c5-9619-01f78db0e2cb]], formerly of [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]. They later record as the bass duo Dos, and stay friends after divorcing.
An SST stopgap EP built around 'Sometimes', one of the songs that later soundtracked Santa Cruz skate videos.

years.h: fROMOHIO: named for Ed Crawford, and their best
years.p: Trouser Press called it the band's best, most accessible record, with country-rock turns like 'Understanding' and 'Vastopol' and a George Hurley drum solo.

years.h: 'Time with You' reaches No. 26 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart
years.p: The Ed Crawford song from fROMOHIO, sent out as an SST promo, becomes fIREHOSE's first chart single.

years.cap: Santa Cruz Skateboards, Streets on Fire
years.h: Santa Cruz skate videos make fIREHOSE a skater band
years.p: 'Brave Captain', 'Sometimes', 'Hear Me' and 'Windmilling' turn up in Santa Cruz Skateboards' Streets on Fire videos, winning fIREHOSE a crowd of underground skaters.

eras.title: Columbia calls
eras.text: In 1991 the most econo band in America signed with Columbia, and its fans braced for a sellout. What they got was two major-label albums, a live record full of covers, and a band that quit on its own terms in its hometown.

q: We make records to promote tours.
years.h: fIREHOSE leaves SST for Columbia Records
years.p: The signing surprises fans, some of whom fear a sellout. Mike Watt's line on the band never changed: they made records to promote tours.

years.h: Flyin' the Flannel, with a Daniel Johnston cover
years.p: Produced with Paul Q. Kolderie at Mad Dog in Venice, faster and heavier than before. Their cover of [[Daniel Johnston|8a7ca8b0-d23c-4eff-8fe9-6220ba5c9c76]]'s 'Walking the Cow' becomes an unlikely hit.

years.h: Live Totem Pole: Public Enemy, Superchunk and Blue Öyster Cult
years.p: A live EP from the Palomino in Los Angeles, stacked with covers of [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]], [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]] and [[Blue Öyster Cult|c7423e0c-ab3e-4ab4-be10-cdff5a9d3062]].

years.h: Mr. Machinery Operator, produced by J Mascis
years.p: Cut at Capitol Studios in Hollywood with [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] producing and guests [[Nels Cline|afa7b889-c499-4194-9367-7b80c9f88325]], Joe Baiza and [[Mac McCaughan|8841967d-3914-4ab9-aca6-94781aa35288]]. It's fIREHOSE's last album.
years.xp: Reviews were cool: Entertainment Weekly called it agreeably sedate, and Robert Christgau called it a dud.

years.h: Last show: the Warner Grand Theatre, San Pedro
years.p: After about 980 gigs in seven and a half years, fIREHOSE ends where it started, in Mike Watt and George Hurley's hometown.
years.xp: Watt went solo on Columbia with Ball-Hog or Tugboat? in 1995 and later played bass for [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]]. [[Ed Crawford|c02f03fe-93cf-4590-841b-1b9f04d6a694]] fronted Grand National and toured as a hired guitarist with [[Whiskeytown|fdb40275-50df-4894-8481-573e86956e81]] and [[Southern Culture on the Skids|90c88f94-8b70-49fd-9726-cadf4306ef42]].

eras.title: Smokin' on the ol' pink pole
eras.text: Eighteen years after the Warner Grand, Mike Watt, George Hurley and Ed Crawford got back in the van for two weeks, with a Columbia anthology to mark it.

years.p: A two-CD anthology of the Columbia albums plus bonus live cuts and instrumentals.

years.h: fIREHOSE reunites at Harlow's in Sacramento
years.p: The 14-date 'Smokin' on the Ol' Pink Pole' tour starts in Sacramento and includes both weekends of Coachella.
